figures.caption: Table 1: Comparison of representative non-invasive AAD datasets. MOV-AAD uniquely combines dynamic spatial movement, conversational speech, and synchronized multimodal physiological recordings under ecologically realistic conditions.
Table 2: Dataset summary. Key parameters of the MOV-AAD dataset, including modalities, tasks, and stimulus configuration.

Figure 1: Overview of the MOV-AAD dataset and experimental paradigm. Left: Multimodal recording setup and example for synchronized signal traces. Right: Full experimental pipeline and stimuli description.

Figure 2: Localization Perception. Top: Localization patterns visualized in polar coordinates. For each subject, perceived angles were averaged for each true angle. Gray open circles denote true stimulus angles, and colored markers represent the acrosssubject average perceived angle for each true angle. Bottom panels compare high-accuracy (top 33% of subjects by localization accuracy) and low-accuracy (bottom 33%) groups, highlighting slight differences in localization profiles. Bottom: Subject-level localization performance. Gray bars indicate localization accuracy, and red bars indicate mean absolute localization error. Subjects are sorted by accuracy. Dashed lines denote chance level (accuracy = 11.11%, black; mean absolute error ≈ 66.7◦ for the -90◦ to 90◦ range with nine response options, red).

Figure 3: Repeated-word detection performance in the conversation tasks. Left: behavioral map showing precision vs. hit rate for single-conversation (SC), multi-conversation attended (MC-A), and multi-conversation unattended (MC-U). Right: F1-score across tasks/streams. Asterisks denote significant paired differences (two-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test, ∗p < 0.05,∗∗p < 0.01,∗∗∗p < 0.001); the corresponding rankbased effect size r is annotated.

Figure 4: Physiological data sanity check. Each panel shows distributions of physiological features (boxplots; median in blue). Gray dots represent participants. Orange dashed lines indicate expected physiological ranges based on prior literature and device specifications.

Figure 5: Stimulus reconstruction correlation and AAD accuracy across window sizes. Sliding-window reconstruction was performed within each trial (hop size = 0.5 s). Left: Reconstruction correlations for attended (rA) and unattended (rU ) streams as a function of window size. Correlations are averaged across windows and trials per subject, then across subjects (mean ± 95% CI). Right: AAD accuracy as a function of window size. For each subject and trial, accuracy was defined as the proportion of windows with rA > rU . Subject-level accuracy was obtained by averaging across trials, and the plotted curve shows the across-subject mean ± 95% CI. Colors indicate feature type. Chance level (0.5) is indicated by the dashed line.

Figure 7: Full-trial LDA decoding across feature types. LDA accuracy for envelope, trajectory (delta/alpha), and combined feature sets. Accuracy reflects the proportion of correctly classified held-out trials under leave-one-trial-out cross-validation. Each box shows the median and interquartile range across subjects. The dashed line indicates permutation-based chance level estimated separately for each feature condition (1000 label shuffles). Statistical significance was assessed using one-sample right-tailed t-tests against subject-specific null means, with multiple comparisons corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Asterisks denote significant above-chance decoding (* p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001).

Figure 8: Intersubject correlation across modalities. For each modality, trial-wise ISC was computed and averaged across trials to obtain one ISC value per subject. Chance level was estimated from a subject-specific permutation null distribution and summarized in the same manner. Boxes show the median and interquartile range across subjects; paired lines connect each subject’s ISC to its chance baseline (blue: subject-level significant difference from the null, p < 0.05, permutation test; gray: n.s.). Group-level significance was assessed using a paired right-tailed test across subjects comparing ISC to chance (for each modality, a paired t-test was used when ISC-chance differences passed a Lilliefors normality test; otherwise a Wilcoxon signed-rank test was applied). To quantify prevalence, we counted the number of subjects with permutation test p < 0.05 and evaluated whether this count exceeded the expected false-positive rate using a binomial test (reported in each panel). Statistical significance: * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001.
